sections: What stays code in the standalone module

items.text: Gap 1: a slot that reads a YAML scalar as written
Gap 2: a rule chosen by a value
Gap 3: the indentation indicator of a block scalar
items.reason: FBL 6.3 states no indentation indicator for a literal block whose first line begins with a space, so the yaml family writes `|-` and the body no longer reads; the description cannot state the repair until FBL does.

items.text: Gap 4: opening an empty flow collection
Gap 5: a removal that leaves the comment above
items.reason: A binding's `remove` has no option that leaves the leading comments of the entry it removes; the standalone stand-in FdgCommentKeeper does it in code.

items.text: Gap 6: the wording of a body that cannot be read and of a planner's refusal
items.reason: A binding cannot word what its reader reports or its planner refuses; `std.unreadableEntry` passes the reader's reason through, and the tool's own sentences come from FdgReaderSentences.

items.text: Gap 7: which relation a pointer gesture creates
Gap 8: an order of findings that is not by code and then by line
items.reason: `constraints.order` orders by code and then by line; an order per code, by document, by relation or by line, is not stated in DISL or ATD (the owner's ruling of 2026-10-11 keeps today's order).

items.text: **Within `fdg.unreadable-entry`**, the findings come in reading order: elements, then connections, then the header.
items.reason: Reading order within one code is the gap 8 construct.

items.text: **Across the link codes**, one finding per connection in document order, mixing `fdg.dangling-reference`, `fdg.self-link` and `fdg.forbidden-link`
items.reason: Document order across several codes is the gap 8 construct.

items.text: **For cardinality**, by relation in the order the notation lists the relations
items.reason: An order by relation is the gap 8 construct.

items.text: Gap 9: a size clamped on commit
Gap 10: a number written in quotes
items.reason: A binding slot cannot state its own number conversion and fallback (a value that does not convert kept at a default and reported), so the binding reads the text and FdgReading converts it.

items.text: Gap 11: the id an unresolved end was written with
items.reason: CEL sees an unresolved end as absent and cannot read the id it was written with; `sourceId` and `targetId` on a relation would state it.

items.text: Gap 12: the detail and place of a cycle and of a cardinality finding
a loop as "Ownership loops: a -> b -> a.", the members rotated to start at the least id, one finding per elementary loop, on the line of that least-id member
a cardinality breach on the line of the last connection over the limit.
items.reason: `std.multiplicity` states no location for its findings, and a built-in's setting cannot name one; DISL 8.7 leaves it to the runtime.

items.text: Gap 13: the indentation of a new entry
Gap 14: the sign of a number that rounds to zero
items.statedBy: binding fdg element ui-element attribute x

hostCode.behaviour: A body is read without ever failing: a text that is not YAML is an empty model with the reason and its line, an unknown key, type or malformed entry is kept and reported, a coordinate that does not read is zero and reported.
A position or a size is read from any scalar in the invariant culture (`"120"` is 120, `1e2` is 100), and one that does not read is zero with a finding.
hostCode.divergesFrom: binding fdg element ui-element attribute x

hostCode.behaviour: A Comment is drawn at least 48 high, and an element of an unknown type is kept and drawn as nothing.
A new element is named for its type (`New UI element`, `New action`, `New data element`, `New function`), with ` 2`, ` 3` and so on until no element has the name.

Each edit (add, connect, disconnect, remove, rename, describe, place, size) is one splice of the body's lines, run on a copy so that a refusal leaves nothing; removing an element removes its connections in the same step.
Every edit is one command on the project's history whose undo restores the text the body held before.
hostCode.reason: The history and how an exact undo is kept are the host's; the description says each gesture is one command (ATD 12.4).

hostCode.behaviour: An element's menu is Rename (Edit text on a Comment, F2) and Remove (Delete); a connection's is Rename and Remove connection; empty canvas offers one Add per type; a finished connect offers all five relations.
Removing an element asks first only when connections go with it, naming how many ("Removing this element also removes the 1 connection to or from it.").

A Name for the four named types and a connection, a Text for a Comment instead, a Description for every element and connection, and Width, with a Comment's Height, shown as the file holds them to four decimals.
A size that is not a positive number is refused before any command exists: "'x' is not a size this graph can draw.".
A drag from one element's body to another's draws the one relation whose ends admit the pair.
Ownership loops are found by a depth-first walk over the four ownership relations, Shows exempt, each loop once and rotated to start at its least id.
An ownership link closes a loop when its owner is already reachable from what it would own.
A connect is checked for type, then cardinality, then cycle, each refusal naming its check; a relation the notation does not have and an end that is gone are refused in the tool's words.
The rules are reported in rule order and then document order: duplicate ids, unreadable entries, links, cardinality, cycles.
One link finding per connection in document order: dangling, then self, then unknown relation, then the pair.
A cardinality breach is reported per relation in the notation's order, on the line of the last connection over the limit.
One finding per ownership loop, "Ownership loops: a -> b -> a.", on the line of its first member.
What a rule would refuse is still drawn; an entry of an unknown type, a connection whose end is not an element and a later holder of an id already drawn are not.
hostCode.reason: Which reading entries the canvas draws, and the payload it is sent, are the host's drawing; the description's notation draws every element and relation of the model.

hostCode.behaviour: The palette's five tools, each dropped centred on the point it lands at.
A Comment reads as its first line in the selection, an element as its name, a connection as its name or its ends.
A line spliced in takes the line ending most of the document's lines use, CRLF on a tie.
